title: architecture review - routing policy + fallback notes (kv cache) 2026-04-12
content:
Context:
We held an architecture review to decide on the routing policy and fallback behavior for requests that miss in the KV prefix cache and/or when a model variant is unavailable. This is a follow-up to RFC #142 (KV cache sharding) and last week's multi-route notes. Goal: land on a default routing policy that balances latency SLOs, cost, and consistency of outputs, and define an operational rollout path.

Attendees:
- Priya Ramesh (owner)
- Ethan Morales
- Lina Chen
- Jonas Becker
- Marta Silva
- Notes: remote attendees joined on Slack thread #serving-runtime-arch

Summary / TL;DR:
- Agreed to adopt a prioritized routing policy: primary route -> fast-fallback route -> compatible-model fallback -> queue/buffer with graceful degradation.
- For KV cache misses, prefer a local-prefetch attempt + immediate fallthrough to the serving node's model instance (no cross-node fetch synchronously).
- Implement a probabilistic early-fallback for high-p99 latency risk windows (configurable per-route).
- Rollout plan: staged feature flag in Dedicated first (canary customer), then Hosted API internal clients, then global rollout with metrics gating.

Discussion notes:
1) Routing priority stack
   - Primary route: exact model + route pinned by customer. Strong requirement for determinism; should be first attempt.
   - Fast-fallback route: model variant with same architecture/quantization that is on the same locality (same machine/cluster) to avoid cross-region hops. Use when primary capacity is saturated or p99 latency breaches.
   - Compatible-model fallback: broader set, may change output semantics slightly (e.g., different tokenizer behavior). This requires informing customers via rollout notice and offering toggle.
   - Final fallback: queue/slowpath where requests are buffered and served with a guarantee (best-effort) - exposes longer latency but preserves correctness.

2) KV cache miss behavior
   - We debated synchronously fetching missing prefixes from other shards. Consensus: avoid synchronous cross-shard fetch in the hot path due to unpredictable tail latency and network variance.
   - Preferred approach: local prefetch (if neighboring cache lines exist) + local model execution. Insert asynchronous cross-shard prefetch to populate caches for future requests.
   - Eviction interplay: if a miss causes a spike and misses are frequent, circuit-break into early-fallback to protect downstream latency.

3) Probabilistic early-fallback (PEF)
   - Implement a lightweight sampler that on high load chooses fast-fallback with X% probability for non-critical user types. Configurable by route and customer tier.
   - Rationale: reduces p99 by preemptively avoiding slow tails, helps stable autoscaler signals.

4) Consistency and reproducibility concerns
   - Compatible-model fallback changes output distribution. We must record which fallback was used in trace metadata and provide a flag to disable compatibility fallback per customer.
   - For deterministic replay/evals, default path must be pinned to primary model version; fallbacks should be opt-in for replay.

5) Observability and instrumentation
   - Add metrics: fallback_type (enum), fallback_latency, cache_miss_reason (evicted|cold|shard-miss), prefetch_hit_rate, early_fallback_sample_rate, and per-route p50/p90/p99 split by fallback_type.
   - Tracing: include fallback decision in trace spans and log the exact route/model_version used.

6) Rollout and risk mitigation
   - Start in Dedicated with one canary customer and synthetic load tests. Gate on p99 latency, error rate, and quality regression (measured via stored prompt-set evals).
   - Deploy PEF as off by default; enable only in controlled experiments.
   - Feature flags: route-level toggles + global kill-switch.

Decisions made (explicit):
- Default routing policy = primary -> local fast-fallback -> compatible-model -> queued slowpath. (PRIORITY)
- Synchronous cross-shard KV fetches are disallowed in the hot path.
- Implement asynchronous cross-shard prefetch to populate caches post-miss.
- Instrument fallback_type and expose via Console.
- PEF allowed but behind flag; sample rate configurable by tenant.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Exact heuristics for when to prefer compatible-model fallback vs queued slowpath. (ACTION: define threshold equations; owner: Lina)
- Token-level cost accounting when using fallback model variants (how to reflect on billing/console). (ACTION: Finance stub + Ethan to propose billing tag approach)
- Prefetch coordination: should we coordinate a background sync across shards every N seconds for hot prefixes? Tradeoffs with network cost. (ACTION: Jonas to prototype with simulated traffic)

Action items / owners:
- Lina: Draft threshold heuristic doc for fallback decision (deadline 2026-04-19).
- Jonas: Prototype cross-shard async prefetch simulation and cost estimate (deadline 2026-04-22).
- Ethan: Proposal for billing/console exposure for fallback model usage (deadline 2026-04-18).
- Priya: Set up canary Dedicated config and synthetic load harness (deadline 2026-04-20).
- Marta: Add metrics/tracing spec and begin instrumentation PR (depends on routes API changes) (deadline 2026-04-21).

Notes to implementation team (dev-friendly):
- See KV cache RFC #142 for existing shard map and eviction semantics; this work assumes the shard map and virtual slots are stable.
- When implementing PEF, prefer a low-cost RNG and sample at request ingress to minimize overhead.
- Traces must include a "fallback_reason" tag and "route_chosen" to make debugging easier for CS and customers.

Follow-ups / meeting cadence:
- Sync next on 2026-04-19 to review Lina's threshold heuristics and Ethan's billing proposal.
- Weekly check-ins until rollout reaches hosted internal customers.
